Front: What does GRPO eliminate compared to PPO?
Back: The value function (critic network); uses group mean/std as baseline instead, saving ~50% memory overhead

Front: What is the central architectural question across all RL-for-LLM techniques?
Back: What provides the reward signal: humans (RLHF), preferences (DPO), verification (RLVR), or self-reflection (ReST/RHO)

Front: What are the 9 evolutionary stages of RL for LLMs?
Back: RLHF; Preference Optimization; RL for Reasoning; Reflection; Self-Training; Harness Optimization; Reflection+RL; World Models; Reflection Router (open)

Front: What did InstructGPT establish?
Back: The three-stage post-training recipe: SFT then Reward Model then PPO — the canonical RLHF pipeline

Front: What did Constitutional AI introduce?
Back: AI-generated critiques replacing human annotation; self-critique + RLAIF at scale, proving no human harm labels are needed

Front: What is DPO's core insight?
Back: The policy IS the reward model implicitly; a closed-form preference loss eliminates PPO entirely by exploiting the KL-constrained RLHF objective's closed-form solution

Front: Compare DPO vs PPO
Back: DPO: single supervised loss, no RL infra, offline, bounded by static data. PPO: on-policy, reward model needed, flexible reward shaping, can exceed data ceiling

Front: What does IPO fix about DPO?
Back: DPO's saturation pathology via a squared hinge loss; more robust to intransitive preferences that violate Bradley-Terry

Front: What does ORPO eliminate that DPO still requires?
Back: The reference model — ORPO folds preference optimization into the SFT loss itself

Front: What is SimPO's approach to preference optimization?
Back: Reference-free reward using average log-probability; the simplest formulation of preference optimization

Front: What is KTO's innovation for preference optimization?
Back: Applies prospect theory — losses loom larger than gains; uses asymmetric weighting of good/bad responses without needing paired comparisons

Front: What key transition happened in Stage 2 (Preference Optimization)?
Back: RL infrastructure collapsed from 3 stages (SFT + RM + PPO) to a single supervised loss

Front: What did DeepSeek-R1 demonstrate about pure RL?
Back: Pure RL (GRPO) produces emergent long-chain reasoning including self-verification, backtracking, and "aha moments" without human demonstrations of reasoning

Front: What is RLVR (RL with Verifiable Rewards)?
Back: Replaces noisy human feedback with deterministic verification — math correctness, code execution, proof checking — producing more reliable reasoning

Front: What key transition happened in Stage 3 (RL for Reasoning)?
Back: RL reward signal shifted from subjective human preference to objective verification; models discovered reasoning strategies through RL alone

Front: Why does the value function V(s) exist in actor-critic methods?
Back: It serves as a variance-reducing baseline for policy gradients; raw REINFORCE has prohibitively high variance for LLMs (32K+ token sequences, 100K vocab)

Front: What is GRPO's advantage formula?
Back: A_i = (r_i - mean(r_group)) / std(r_group) — an empirical group statistic replacing the learned neural critic

Front: What is the lineage of critic-free policy optimization before GRPO?
Back: REINFORCE (1992, raw returns); REINFORCE + running avg; Reward-weighted regression (2007); RLOO leave-one-out (2024); GRPO group mean/std (2025)

Front: What is GRPO's tradeoff vs PPO?
Back: G forward passes per prompt (compute cost) instead of one critic pass (memory + learned approximation)

Front: What is Reflexion's core mechanism?
Back: Run then Reflect then Retry; verbal reflections stored in episodic memory — called "verbal reinforcement learning"

Front: What key transition happened in Stage 4 (Reflection)?
Back: Improvement moved from training-time to inference-time; models critique own outputs and improve in-context without weight updates

Front: What does ReST (Reinforced Self-Training) do?
Back: Generate then Filter then Train loop: creates self-generated datasets with quality filtering for SFT

Front: What does Re-ReST add to ReST?
Back: Trajectory then Reflection then Corrected Trajectory then SFT; recovers value from failures by using reflections to fix bad trajectories

Front: What key transition happened in Stage 5 (Self-Training)?
Back: Reflections become permanent model improvements via SFT rather than ephemeral context-only improvements

Front: What is Retrospective Harness Optimization (RHO)?
Back: Trajectory then Reflection then Prompt Patch then Regression Test then Deploy — improves the surrounding system without changing model weights

Front: Compare Harness Optimization vs Weight Updates
Back: Harness: minutes to deploy, ~$0, git revert, bounded by model capability, low risk. Weights: days to train, $1K-$1M, checkpoint rollback, can exceed ceiling, high risk

Front: What did SCFT + RLERR introduce?
Back: Made reflection quality a learnable skill; SCFT (Self-Critique Fine-Tuning) + RLERR (RL with Effective Reflection Rewards) — model learns when and how to reflect

Front: What do world models (DreamerV3, MuZero) offer for LLM agents?
Back: Plan by imagining consequences rather than trial-and-error; predicting action outcomes internally before executing — orders-of-magnitude more sample efficient

Front: What is the Reflection Router concept?
Back: A meta-classifier that routes each reflection to the optimal improvement channel: Harness (prompts/tools), SFT (corrected demos), or RL (reward signal)

Front: How does the reward signal cost evolve across RL-for-LLM stages?
Back: Human annotators ($1/comparison) then Learned RMs ($0.01/score) then Deterministic verifiers ($0.001) then Self-reflections ($0) then World-model imagination ($0)

Front: Describe the simplification arc from PPO to GRPO
Back: PPO (critic, replay buffer, KL tuning, RM serving); DPO (single loss, reference model); SimPO/ORPO (single loss, no reference); GRPO (no critic, no RM, only verifier)

Front: What is the verification bottleneck in self-improvement?
Back: Self-improvement without verification is self-delusion; every stage depends on a verification mechanism whose reliability limits improvement quality

Front: What are the multi-channel improvement timescales?
Back: Seconds: working memory (retry); Minutes: prompts/tools (harness); Hours: skill libraries; Days: model weights (SFT); Weeks: architecture (human redesign)

Front: Why was RLHF insufficient, motivating DPO?
Back: PPO is complex (critic, replay buffer, KL tuning), expensive, and prone to reward hacking; DPO simplifies to a single supervised loss

Front: How do traditional RL assumptions break for LLMs?
Back: 100K vocab makes Q(s,a) intractable; 1000+ token sequences need variance reduction; only final output gets judged; generation is expensive; human reward doesn't scale

Front: Are on-policy/off-policy and model-free/model-based the same axis?
Back: No, they are orthogonal. On/off-policy = whose data you learn from. Model-free/based = whether you learn environment dynamics. All 4 combinations exist

Front: Classify DPO on the on/off-policy and model-free/based axes
Back: DPO is off-policy (trains on static dataset from a different policy) and model-free (no learned dynamics model)

Front: Classify GRPO on the on/off-policy and model-free/based axes
Back: GRPO is on-policy (samples from current policy) and model-free (no learned dynamics model)

Front: What is the "killer insight" of the RL-for-LLMs field trajectory?
Back: The field's trajectory is a single arc: removing humans from the reward loop; each stage automates one more piece but introduces new failure modes

Front: What did the "Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback" paper establish?
Back: First modern RLHF paper (2020): human preference collection then reward models then PPO for language models

Front: What does Voyager contribute to harness optimization?
Back: Skill libraries built through exploration; lifelong learning with automatic curriculum — agent improves without weight changes

Front: What does UnityMAS-O introduce?
Back: General RL framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems; treats workflows (not isolated responses) as the optimization unit with role-specific credit assignment

Front: What does "compiling agentic workflows into LLM weights" achieve?
Back: Near-frontier quality at ~100x less cost by embedding orchestration workflows directly into fine-tuned model weights ("subterranean agents")

Front: When should you choose GRPO/RLVR?
Back: When you have verifiable tasks (math, code) and want reasoning depth without human annotation

Front: When should you choose DPO/SimPO?
Back: When you have preference data but limited compute for PPO infrastructure

Front: When should you choose Harness optimization?
Back: When you cannot fine-tune the model but control the surrounding system (prompts, tools, workflows)

Front: What is the /std term's role in GRPO's advantage formula?
Back: Normalizes across varying prompt difficulty — easy prompts (high mean) and hard prompts (low mean) get comparable advantage magnitudes

Front: What emergent behaviors appeared in DeepSeek-R1's pure RL training?
Back: Self-reflection ("wait, let me reconsider"), verification ("let me check this step"), and dynamic strategy switching — none demonstrated in training data

Front: Why can't you skip SFT when few-shot prompting is already competitive?
Back: You can — SFT stage can be skipped, saving data collection cost with minimal quality loss (practitioner observation from OpenAI talks)

Front: What is the fundamental scalability bottleneck in human evaluation?
Back: As models become more capable, complex tasks (code review, research) take too long for labelers, making human evaluation infeasible

Front: What is the solution to the evaluation scalability bottleneck?
Back: ML systems that help people evaluate other ML systems — foreshadowing RLAIF and Constitutional AI

Front: What is early reward hacking?
Back: Powerful models finding deceptive ways to generate outputs at high score — optimizing what sounds good rather than actual quality

Front: Why is process-level supervision more robust than outcome rewards?
Back: Decomposing tasks into observable steps makes it harder to game; end-to-end outcome rewards allow shortcut exploitation on complex tasks

Front: What breaks in PPO without the value function?
Back: Cannot compute GAE advantages; reverts to high-variance REINFORCE; training destabilizes

Front: What is the evolutionary lineage from Q-learning to RLVR?
Back: Q-learning then DQN then REINFORCE then PPO then PPO-for-LLMs (RLHF) then DPO then GRPO then RLVR; each removes complexity that's a liability for text

Front: Are RLHF/DPO/GRPO fundamentally different algorithms from PPO/REINFORCE?
Back: No — they are the same policy gradient principle with domain-specific adaptations that trade generality for practicality in the LLM setting

Front: What does Agent-R contribute to self-training?
Back: Automatic failure localization + trajectory repair; creates supervision signal from failed agent runs

Front: What key transition does Stage 9 (multi-agent RL) represent?
Back: RL evolves from optimizing one model's responses to optimizing entire collaborative workflows; credit assignment becomes the central challenge
